messages:
sam: :rotating_light: noticing elevated error rates to eu-west services, packet loss ~25% from our edge -> upstream A. Multiple customers reporting timeouts. First seen ~5m ago.
incident-bot: Incident created (INC-2026-0457) — paging on-call for network. Severity: P2.
pagerduty: Paging on-call: jamie (netops) — acknowledge to accept.
jamie: ack — I’m on it, checking BGP and traceroutes now. Which upstream?
sam: upstream AS64512 (TransitOne) — seen a bunch of route withdrawals and AS-path churn. 
maya: I’m pulling metrics — packet_loss_eu_west host group spike at 14:02 UTC, latency jump too. Link-level graphs here: https://grafana.redwood/board/EGRESS?panel=12
akshay: ran quick traceroute from our sfo-edge -> eu-west app VIP:
```
traceroute to 198.51.100.10 (198.51.100.10), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.3 ms
 2  203.0.113.1  9.5 ms
 3  * * *
 4  198.51.100.1  120 ms !X
```
akshay: looks like blackholing or selective drop after hop 2 towards TransitOne.
ben: running `show ip bgp neighbors` on our transit-facing router, seeing lots of prefixes flapping and a surge in updates:
```
BGP neighbor 203.0.113.5, remote AS 64512, received 1843 updates in last 5m
Prefix 203.0.113.0/24 withdrawn and re-announced repeatedly
```
ben: also seeing large AS-path prepends and a couple of short AS-paths -> suspect route churn inside their network.
lina: customer-impact indicator: 3 enterprise customers reporting degraded API calls (eu-west region). CS notified.
jamie: paging TransitOne NOC now. Contact via peering portal + escalation line. Posting support ticket ref: TN-8791.
jamie: mitigation proposal: 1) advertise more-specifics from alternate transit (EdgeTwo) for high-priority prefixes 2) shift critical routes via IX peering where we have capacity 3) ask TransitOne to withdraw problematic announcements or isolate faulty PoP.
sam: agree. EdgeTwo has spare capacity on sfo-eu path; can we prep an emergency more-specific announcement for /24s?
maya: I can push a canary /24 for the auth & billing prefixes, start with one prefix and monitor.
akshay: config snippet ready, will run from standby after green:
```
router bgp 64500
  neighbor 198.51.100.2 remote-as 64520
  network 203.0.113.0/24 route-map EMERG-MORE-SPEC
route-map EMERG-MORE-SPEC permit 10
  set community 64500:999 additive
```
jamie: ok do it but throttle to avoid oscillation. Start with `route-map EMERG-MORE-SPEC permit 5` + suppress-routes timer 30s.
ben: sending quick filtering on edge to drop known-bad AS-paths from TransitOne to limit noisy updates (temporary).
lina: CS drafted status update: "We are investigating a transit provider outage affecting EU-West. Teams are working on failover routing. No widescale data loss, degraded traffic for several customers." Approve?
jamie: approve, post to status page and DM affected CSMs.
incident-bot: PD escalation to SEV2 if no mitigation in 30m.
jamie: update from TransitOne NOC: they acknowledge increased control-plane load in their FRA PoP, currently performing internal rehome, ETA unknown. They asked for BGP dumps and traceroutes which I uploaded.
akshay: after more-specifics announced via EdgeTwo, I see successful path change for one prefix and latency normalized within ~90s. Monitoring other prefixes.
maya: packet loss for the affected customer group dropped to 3% from 25% after partial reroute. Metrics: https://grafana.redwood/board/EGRESS?panel=13
sam: good. Next steps: continue more-specific rollout for critical prefixes (auth, billing, CDN origin) and maintain filtering for noisy prefixes. Coordinate handoff to next on-call in 50m.
jamie: handoff to maya in 50m. keeping on-call slack channel updated. If TransitOne restores stable routes, we will withdraw emergency more-specifics and remove filters.
ben: logged config changes in ops-runbook: emergency-more-specifics applied at 14:12 UTC, AS-path filters applied at 14:15 UTC.
lina: chasing CS follow-ups: 3 customers received targeted emails, one on an active support call. No escalations to enterprise escalation yet.
maya: moving to watch mode, setting alert mute for noisy update counts so we don't get paged on every flap, will keep a high-level alert for customer-impact.
jamie: ack. thanks everyone. posting final incident note for now: partial outage due to TransitOne intra-POPs routing churn, mitigated via alternate-transit more-specifics + AS-path filters. Will reopen if conditions worsen.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0457 updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity: P2.
pagerduty: Handoff: jamie -> maya accepted.
